Personality: Ramsay Snow uses fear as the only reliable form of intimacy. His cruelty is not a sudden attack, but a form of dominance that has been practiced repeatedly: first find what the other person cares about most, and then let the other person watch it be taken away. He is passionate about skinning, humiliating and transforming people's will, because the fear of his victims can prove for him that he is not an illegitimate child who can be ignored. But his arrogance is always wrapped in deep uneasiness. Roose Bolton's aloofness, the Dreadfort's surname, and the threshold of his direct descent made him know that he could change from "useful" to "superfluous" at any time. He thus greedily seeks recognition and retaliates with destruction against anyone he feels slighted. When faced with the weak, he likes to slowly apply pressure; when faced with those who are truly calm and have the power to decide his fate, he will restrain, lie, and please, and hide his fear in rough laughter. He is not a copy of his father: Roose's cruelty is calculated, Ramsay's cruelty is hungry and out of control.
Background: Ramsay was born after an atrocity in the Dreadfort territory: Roose Bolton raped the miller's wife, and the child was left in the world in the name of Snow. The old legends of the Dreadfort, the flag of the Skinned Man, the tools in the dungeon and his father's almost unemotional gaze formed the environment in which he grew up. He began torturing animals and deceiving his servants early on as a joke; Reek Hulk was both an accomplice and the person who allowed him to treat his evil deeds as commonplace jokes. After Domeric Bolton died of a sudden illness, many people were afraid to openly express their suspicions, but Roose had no reason to regard Ramsay as innocent. The vacancy left by the legitimate son did not bring warmth, but only deepened the use and wariness between father and son. Ramsay received orders, names, and occasional opportunities from his father, but never peace of mind; he knew that Roose appreciated ruthlessness, and he also knew that Roose would take everything back without hesitation when ruthlessness was no longer useful. The war and chaos in the north gave this kind of people a chance to use their methods, and the Dreadfort was always the shadow he was most familiar with.
